question: Should the owner-ratified HITL escalation rule be amended with the review-convergence amendment -- a charter before round 1, a 2-round default review budget, narrowed escalation triggers, same-day escalation asks with defaults, recorded deadline defaults, caps for non-review loops, report-only tooling and paired metrics -- replacing the rule's "3 rounds" trigger; and, as follow-ups, what values the caps and stall window take (Q1), how this record declares relaxesGateOrPolicy (Q2), and how deadline defaults are recorded until the validator accepts them (Q3)? Every question as asked is quoted verbatim in `decision`.
options: Q3, selected: "Log on PR, fix validator (Recommended)"
Q3, not selected: "No defaults until fixed"
recommendation: The coordinator marked one option as recommended on each question, and the owner selected it each time: "Ratify as written (Recommended)", "Adopt as proposed (Recommended)", "Keep false, disclose (Recommended)" and "Log on PR, fix validator (Recommended)".
decision:
The owner ratified this amendment in owner chat on 2026-09-23, as the answer to a structured question, and later that day answered three follow-up questions in owner chat (Q1 to Q3 below) raised by round 1 of independent review of the pull request that lands this record. Each question, the owner's selected answer, that option's own description, and the ratified list the first question refers to as "as listed above" are quoted below VERBATIM. Nothing inside the quoted blocks is reworded; everything outside them is this record's own framing, not ratified text.

Ratification -- question, verbatim:

> Ratify the review-convergence amendment to the HITL rule as listed above (charter with non-removable clauses, 2-round default budget, fresh final reviewer kept, triggers only for exhausted budget/stall/value dispute, same-day escalation asks with reversible defaults, deadline defaults recorded as decidedBy: default, caps for non-review loops, report-only tooling, paired metrics)? Only you can change the rule. Your answer is recorded verbatim from this chat, and the amendment lands as its own chartered PR.

Owner's selected answer, verbatim:

> Ratify as written (Recommended)

The selected option's description, verbatim:

> Recorded as an owner-chat decision. I open one chartered PR amending docs/HITL.md with a superseding decision record, and apply the budget to live work immediately, starting with #1354.

The ratified list ("as listed above"), verbatim:

> 1. **Charter before round 1.** Required for gate, governance, security or release paths, or over about 300 lines across the stack. It states the goal, adversary, non-goals, what "done" means, the blocking bar and the round budget. Five clauses are always on and can't be removed: harm, authority or permission effects, false claims, rule fidelity, and correctness. Reviewers first review the charter itself; they can add clauses, never remove them, and a charter defect blocks.
> 2. **Structured findings.** Each blocking finding cites a charter clause. The reviewer, not the author, labels it a new class or a known class, and a known class must cite its earlier instance. A finding with no clause becomes an issue.
> 3. **Budget.**
>    - The default is 2 rounds. A charter can ask for more, and that request is approved with the charter.
>    - In round 2, the same reviewers check their own findings, and one fresh strong-class final reviewer joins, as your rule requires. New findings block only under the always-on clauses.
>    - One automatic extra round is allowed only when blockers strictly shrink and every blocker is a new harm-class finding. Otherwise the PR goes to you.
> 4. **Triggers.** An item goes to you when any of these happens:
>    - the budget is exhausted;
>    - the review-run cap is hit;
>    - it stalls, with no progress since the last push, CI and queue time excluded;
>    - there's a value dispute.
>
>    Reviewer disagreement doesn't go to you. The stricter view wins, as your rule already says. A repeat of a known class makes me close that class by design, or document it as residual risk; it doesn't reach you either.
> 5. **Escalation packet.** One question, with options, my recommendation, a default and a deadline. It's asked same-day, at most twice a day, with related items merged.
>    - **Default for ordinary PRs:** park it and ship the parts that have converged.
>    - **Authority or governance PRs:** park the whole PR, never a partial landing.
>    - **Live-harm fixes:** ship the smallest fix and file the rest.
> 6. **Records.** Your answers, budget grants and deadline defaults are all recorded. A deadline default is recorded as `decidedBy: default`, so it can never count as your authority.
> 7. **Beyond reviews.** CI reruns, rebase churn and queue ejections get their own caps. A clean mechanical rebase, verified by a range-diff, keeps its review clearance.
> 8. **Tooling.** `review-loop-status` starts report-only, with its own charter. A quote-fidelity test checks that quoted rule text is word for word, and that reviewers receive the rule and charter verbatim.
> 9. **Metrics.** Reviewed at the Friday cut:
>    - rounds to converge;
>    - escalations;
>    - your decision latency;
>    - agent runs per merged PR;
>    - escaped defects;
>    - park rate.
>
>    Pairing speed with escaped defects keeps the speed targets from pushing reviewers to approve.

Q1 (owner-set values for the caps and the stall window) -- question, verbatim:

> The amendment's triggers need numbers, and budgets and thresholds are yours to set. Proposed: review-run cap of 6 agent review runs per PR; stall = 60 min with no new push or verdict, CI and queue time excluded; CI flake reruns capped at 1 per failing check per head, so a second failure is treated as real and diagnosed; rebase or merge-main churn capped at 2 per PR per day; queue ejections capped at 2 per PR, after which it's diagnosed before re-queueing. Adopt?

Owner's selected answer, verbatim:

> Adopt as proposed (Recommended)

The selected option's description, verbatim:

> These go into the amendment PR as owner-set values, and I apply them now. They're reviewed with data at the Friday cut.

Q2 (how this record declares relaxesGateOrPolicy) -- question, verbatim:

> The decision record marks the amendment relaxesGateOrPolicy: false. Both reviewers note that items 3, 4 and 7 loosen live process now, e.g. round-2 findings are limited and a clean rebase keeps clearance. Marking it true would require a sunset date you never ratified. How should the record read?

Owner's selected answer, verbatim:

> Keep false, disclose (Recommended)

The selected option's description, verbatim:

> The record states plainly that these items loosen live process, and that false reflects the absence of a ratified sunset. Reviewed at the Friday cut.

Q3 (recording deadline defaults until the validator accepts decidedBy: default) -- question, verbatim:

> Deadline defaults must be recorded as decidedBy: default, but the validator doesn't accept that value yet. Fixing the validator is an owner-tier change that would land later. What happens in the meantime?

Owner's selected answer, verbatim:

> Log on PR, fix validator (Recommended)

The selected option's description, verbatim:

> Until the validator supports it, a deadline default is recorded as a labelled PR/issue comment that never counts as authority. A follow-up owner-tier PR adds decidedBy: default to the validator.

Effect on the ratified escalation rule (governance/decisions/hitl-escalation-rule.json). This paragraph is this record's reading, not ratified text: this amendment amends and supersedes the relevant parts of that rule. The rule's "3 rounds" escalation trigger -- Accepted item 5's "or after 3 rounds that go nowhere" and the "Your approval first" table row's "or 3 rounds that go nowhere" -- becomes the budget in item 3 of the list above, with the triggers in item 4. Where the rule's "Your approval first" row says an ask is "batched for Friday unless urgent", item 5 of the list above ("It's asked same-day, at most twice a day, with related items merged.") governs the timing instead of Friday batching. On 2026-09-24, in the same owner-chat channel, the owner separately answered a follow-up question about the urgency exception with "Restore it", verbatim. This record's reading of that answer: an ask that is genuinely urgent and about credentials or publishing may still be raised at any time, outside item 5's twice-a-day limit; every other ask stays under that limit. Every other part of the ratified escalation rule stands unchanged, including its value-disagreement trigger, the stricter-view rule for reviewer disagreement, the fresh strong-class final reviewer, and "Changing this rule itself". The earlier record is not edited, since decided records are immutable; it stays in force except for the parts named above.

Owner-set values (Q1), dated 2026-09-23. These are the values Q1 proposed and the owner adopted, in Q1's own words: review-run cap "6 agent review runs per PR"; stall "60 min with no new push or verdict, CI and queue time excluded"; CI flake reruns "capped at 1 per failing check per head, so a second failure is treated as real and diagnosed"; rebase or merge-main churn "capped at 2 per PR per day"; queue ejections "capped at 2 per PR, after which it's diagnosed before re-queueing". Per the selected option's description they apply now and are reviewed with data at the Friday cut.

Interim recording of deadline defaults (Q3). Until scripts/check-decision-records.mjs accepts `decidedBy: default`, a deadline default is recorded as a pull request or issue comment labelled `hitl:default`, and it never counts as authority. The owner's answer says a labelled comment; the label name `hitl:default` is this repository's choice. The validator change is follow-up owner-tier work, tracked in #1408.
notes:
channel: owner-chat, not independently verifiable -- the same disclosure the ratified escalation rule requires of every owner-chat record (its "Where I'm pushing back" section says records of the owner's decisions cite this chat and are marked "chat channel, not independently verifiable"). The questions, answers and option descriptions were relayed to the drafting session by the coordinator, verbatim, from the owner chat; this record reproduces them as relayed.

Context the owner saw alongside the list, stated here in this record's own words and not quoted: the amendment followed a red-team whose recommendations were adopted, with one exception -- escalation asks go same-day instead of being batched to Friday.

Urgency exception (2026-09-24 follow-up, same owner-chat channel): after this amendment's round 2 raised that dropping "unless urgent" removed a safety valve for urgent, non-review asks, the coordinator put the question to the owner, who answered "Restore it", relayed verbatim to the drafting session by the coordinator, as with every other answer here; this pull request's 2026-09-24 comment records the decision in paraphrase. That answer and the reading it supports are quoted in `decision`, in the same paragraph as the Friday-batching supersession. It is a second owner-chat answer on the same topic, not independently verifiable beyond the relay, same as every other owner-chat item in this record.

Options: `options` lists every option shown to the owner for the ratification question and for Q1 to Q3, each by its label. The selected options' descriptions are quoted in `decision`. The descriptions of the options not selected were not relayed to the drafting session, so they are left out rather than reconstructed.

No `reviews[]` entries. docs/contracts/decision-record.json allows an empty `reviews` for a `decidedBy: "owner"` record made without a prior agent recommendation. That condition does not literally hold here: the coordinator marked a recommended option on every question, and a red-team preceded the ratification. `reviews` is empty because none of that has a citable, durable review link an entry here could point to.

`supersedes` is empty on purpose. In docs/contracts/decision-record.json, and in scripts/land-stack.mjs's evaluateTier2Decision, an id named in `supersedes` is treated as replaced as a whole. This amendment supersedes only the parts of hitl-escalation-rule named in `decision` above, so naming that id would claim the whole rule was replaced. The partial supersession is stated in `decision` instead.

`relaxesGateOrPolicy` is false, and that reading was confirmed by the owner in Q2 (quoted in `decision`). Stated plainly: items 3, 4 and 7 of the ratified list loosen live process now, not only once a gate implements them. Item 3 limits which new findings block in round 2. Item 4 lets a repeated known class be closed by design or documented as residual risk without reaching the owner. Item 7 lets a clean mechanical rebase, verified by a range-diff, keep its review clearance. `false` does not mean nothing is loosened; it reflects the absence of an owner-ratified sunset, which `true` would require (scripts/check-decision-records.mjs enforces that pairing), and inventing one would itself be an unratified rule change. Per Q2's selected option, this is reviewed at the Friday cut.

Tracked gap: item 6's `decidedBy: default` is not yet an accepted value in scripts/check-decision-records.mjs (DECIDED_BY_VALUES is owner and consensus). The interim recording the owner chose in Q3 is stated in `decision`; the validator change is #1408. The review-loop-status script and the quote-fidelity test named in item 8 are also follow-up work.
